title: Through-Arch Clock Plaza
description: One static public-clock plaza scene for the original timekeeping public-clock program. The complete existing square four-face clock tower retains its genuine front-to-back arched opening and both strip feet, beside two complete original low entry benches placed off the central axis. Every raw legacy GLB vertex/index/normal buffer, internal node, fixed pointer angle and per-face PBR assignment is preserved at unit scale and identity orientation. Only one low connected plaza ground with a straight contrasting central paving band is new scene-only geometry; the ground top stays at the original feet and does not fill the arch. The approach aligns front-to-back with the existing opening, while the separate bench zones and conservative peripheral empty strips provide a distinct axial public-clock layout, not the old tabletop clock-and-sundial display or a renamed fountain plaza. One scene, zero new independent models, three whole instances of two existing types. Whole finite original soles remain on the plaza and whole-instance bounds are separated. Static display only: no timekeeping, chime, mechanism, public passage usability, circulation standard, human ergonomics, load, weather resistance, outdoor suitability, construction or public safety claim.
